'''Jaden Amere Hardy''' (born July 5, 2002) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and one of the top players in the 2021 class.

Instead of playing college basketball, Hardy joined the [[NBA G League Ignite]], a developmental team in the [[NBA G League]], in 2021. He was drafted in the second round of the [[2022 NBA draft]] and played for the [[Dallas Mavericks]] for four seasons, with whom he reached the [[2024 NBA Finals]]. He was traded to the [[Washington Wizards]] during the 2025–26 season, and then to the Lakers during the 2026 off-season.

==Early life==
Hardy and his family moved to [[Henderson, Nevada]] from [[Detroit]], before high school.<ref>{{cite web |last=Richey |first=Scott |title=Las Vegas to C-U connection? Underwood all in on Hardy |url=https://www.news-gazette.com/sports/illini-sports/las-vegas-to-c-u-connection-underwood-all-in-on-hardy/article_1799aab6-20ab-58ad-b870-4cff08357aed.html |website=[[The News-Gazette (Champaign–Urbana)|The News-Gazette]] |access-date=April 19, 2021 |date=May 7, 2018}}</ref> He attended [[Coronado High School (Nevada)|Coronado High School]] in Henderson. As a junior, Hardy averaged 30.4 points, 9.1 rebounds and 8.4 assists per game, earning Nevada [[Gatorade Player of the Year awards|Gatorade Player of the Year]] and ''[[Las Vegas Review-Journal]]'' Boys Athlete of the Year honors.<ref>{{cite web |last=Grimala |first=Mike |title=Two prep athletes who dominated the competition |url=https://lasvegassun.com/news/2020/may/24/two-prep-athletes-who-dominated-the-competition/ |website=[[Las Vegas Sun]] |access-date=April 19, 2021 |date=May 24, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Orts |first=Jason |title=Nevada Preps awards – Boys Athlete of the Year |url=https://www.reviewjournal.com/nevada-preps/np-basketball/boys-basketball/nevada-preps-awards-boys-athlete-of-the-year-2038791/ |website=[[Las Vegas Review-Journal]] |access-date=April 19, 2021 |date=May 29, 2020}}</ref> On January 8, 2021, he opted out from the remainder of his senior season.<ref>{{cite web |last=Jordan |first=Jason |title=SI99 No. 1 SG Jaden Hardy No Longer Playing This Season |url=https://www.si.com/college/recruiting/basketball/jaden-hardy-coronado-si99-2021-not-playing-high-school |website=[[Sports Illustrated]] |access-date=April 19, 2021 |date=January 8, 2021}}</ref> He was named to the rosters for the [[2021 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|McDonald's All-American Game]], [[Jordan Brand Classic]] and [[Nike Hoop Summit]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Brewer |first=Ray |title=Even without season, Coronado's Jaden Hardy named McDonald's All-American |url=https://lasvegassun.com/news/2021/feb/23/even-without-season-coronados-jaden-hardy-named-mc/ |website=[[Las Vegas Sun]] |access-date=April 19, 2021 |date=February 23, 2021}}</ref>

Hardy was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and one of the best players in the 2021 class.{{Cn|date=July 2026}} Most recruiting analysts predicted that he would play professionally instead of attending college, with [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]] and [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA]] being his most likely college destinations.<ref>{{cite web |last=Roberts |first=Ben |title=More buzz indicating a top Kentucky basketball target will skip college for the pros |url=https://www.kentucky.com/sports/college/kentucky-sports/uk-recruiting/next-cats-blog/article250141824.html |website=[[Lexington Herald-Leader]] |access-date=April 19, 2021 |date=March 23, 2021}}</ref> On May 15, 2021, he announced that he would join the [[NBA G League]], forgoing college basketball. He chose the G League over offers from Kentucky and UCLA, among others.{{Cn|date=July 2026}}

==Professional career==
===NBA G League Ignite (2021–2022)===
On June 9, 2021, Hardy signed with the [[NBA G League Ignite]], a developmental team affiliated with the [[NBA G League]].<ref>{{cite web |date=June 9, 2021 |title=Five-Star Prospect Jaden Hardy Signs With NBA G League Ignite |url=https://gleague.nba.com/news/five-star-prospect-jaden-hardy-signs-with-nba-g-league-ignite/ |access-date=June 12, 2021 |website=gleague.nba.com}}</ref> He averaged 17.7 points, 4.6 rebounds and 3.2 assists per game, shooting 35.1 percent from the field.<ref>{{cite web |last=Pompey |first=Keith |title=Sixers work out G League Ignite guard Jaden Hardy ahead of Thursday's NBA draft |url=https://www.inquirer.com/sixers/jaden-hardy-works-out-for-sixers-nba-draft-20220620.html |website=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]] |access-date=June 22, 2022 |date=June 20, 2022}}</ref>

===Dallas Mavericks (2022–2026)===
Hardy was drafted 37th in the [[2022 NBA draft]] by the [[Sacramento Kings]], and traded on draft night to the [[Dallas Mavericks]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=June 23, 2022 |title=Kings Acquire Two Future Second-Round Draft Picks From Dallas |url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-acquire-two-future-second-round-draft-picks-from-dallas |access-date=June 24, 2022 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> He joined the Mavericks for the [[2022 NBA Summer League]]. On July 7, 2022, Hardy made his Summer League debut against the [[2022–23 Chicago Bulls season|Chicago Bulls]] with 28 points, four rebounds, three assists, and one steal in a 100–99 loss.<ref>{{cite web |last=Guinhawa |first=Angelo |date=July 8, 2022 |title=Jaden Hardy's stern message after setting NBA Summer League on fire with 28-point debut for Mavs |url=https://clutchpoints.com/mavs-news-jaden-hardy-stern-message-after-setting-nba-summer-league-on-fire-with-28-point-debut/ |access-date=July 11, 2022 |website=ClutchPoints}}</ref> On February 6, 2023, he scored a career-high 29 points in a 124–111 win over the [[2022–23 Utah Jazz season|Utah Jazz]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sefko |first=Eddie |title=MAVERICKS, FEELING DISRESPECTED, STUN JAZZ WITH MAKESHIFT LINEUP, 124–111 |url=https://www.mavs.com/mavs-shock-jazz |website=Dallas Mavericks |access-date=February 6, 2023 |date=February 6, 2023}}</ref> On March 11, Hardy started his first game in the NBA, recording 22 points, two rebounds and three assists in a 112–108 loss to the [[2022–23 Memphis Grizzlies season|Memphis Grizzlies]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bailey |first=Clay |date=March 11, 2023 |title=RODDY LEADS FOURTH-QUARTER RALLY AS GRIZZLIES BEAT MAVERICKS |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022201010 |access-date=March 16, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> He made 48 total appearances (including five starts) for Dallas during his rookie campaign, recording averages of 8.8 points, 1.9 rebounds, and 1.4 assists.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Jaden Hardy 2022–23 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4868423/type/nba/year/2023|access-date=March 7, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref>

Hardy made 73 appearances (including seven starts) for the Mavericks during the [[2023–24 NBA season]], averaging 7.3 points, 1.8 rebounds, and 1.5 assists.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Jaden Hardy 2023–24 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4868423/type/nba/year/2024|access-date=March 7, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref> Hardy reached the [[2024 NBA Finals]] where the Mavericks lost to the [[Boston Celtics]] in five games.<ref>{{cite web |date=June 17, 2024 |title=Boston Celtics defeat Dallas Mavericks to win 2024 NBA Finals |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/boston-celtics-beat-dallas-mavericks-2024-nba-finals/ |access-date=June 17, 2024 |publisher=cbsnews.com}}</ref>

Prior to the start of the [[2024–25 NBA season]], Hardy signed a three-year, $18 million extension that would keep him under contract through 2028.<ref>{{cite web |date=October 21, 2024 |title=Sources: Mavericks, Jaden Hardy reach 3-year, $18M extension |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/41933469/dallas-mavericks-jaden-hardy-reach-3-year-extension |access-date=April 17, 2026 |publisher=espn.com}}</ref> Hardy played in 57 games (including three starts) for Dallas during the regular season, averaging 8.7 points, 1.6 rebounds, and 1.4 assists.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Jaden Hardy 2024–25 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4868423/type/nba/year/2025|access-date=March 7, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref>

Hardy made 34 appearances (including four starts) for the Mavericks during the [[2025–26 NBA season]], recording averages of 6.9 points, 1.4 rebounds, and 0.9 assists.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Jaden Hardy 2025-26 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4868423/jaden-hardy|access-date=June 25, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref>

===Washington Wizards (2026)===
On February 5, 2026, Hardy was traded to the [[Washington Wizards]] in a three-team trade involving the [[Charlotte Hornets]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/news/wizards-acquire-10-time-all-star-anthony-davis|title=Wizards Acquire 10-Time All-Star Anthony Davis  |work=[[NBA.com]]|date=February 5, 2026}}</ref> On February 11, Hardy made his debut with the Wizards, where he tallied up 11 points, two rebounds, and one assist in 15 minutes of gameplay in a 138–113 loss against the [[2025–26 Cleveland Cavaliers season|Cleveland Cavaliers]]. He made 23 appearances for Washington, logging averages of 12.6 points, 1.7 rebounds, and 1.3 assists.

===Los Angeles Lakers (2026–present)===

On July 7, 2026, Hardy, along with two future picks was traded to the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] in exchange for [[Deandre Ayton]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Los Angeles Lakers Acquire Guard Jaden Hardy|date=July 7, 2026|publisher=Los Angeles Lakers|url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/news/lakers-acquire-guard-jaden-hardy|access-date=July 7, 2026}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Hardy's older brother, [[Amauri Hardy|Amauri]], played college basketball for [[UNLV Runnin' Rebels basketball|UNLV]] and the [[Oregon Ducks men's basketball|University of Oregon]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Gordon |first=Sam |title=Coronado's Jaden Hardy emerges as one of nation's top 9th-grade players |url=https://www.reviewjournal.com/nevada-preps/coronados-jaden-hardy-emerges-as-one-of-nations-top-9th-grade-players/ |website=[[Las Vegas Review-Journal]] |access-date=April 19, 2021 |date=November 28, 2017}}</ref> His father, Ramsey, was on [[Tuskegee Golden Tigers|Tuskegee University]]'s basketball team.<ref>{{cite web |last=Bennett |first=Brian |title=Recruiting notebook: Jaden Hardy has his sights set on being No. 1 in '21 |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/1964533/2020/07/31/recruiting-notebook-jaden-hardy-has-his-sights-set-on-being-no-1-in-21/ |website=[[The Athletic]] |access-date=April 19, 2021 |date=July 31, 2020}}</ref>
